q: Does the paper's Fig. 6 best-practice phase-diagram boundary between Linear, Quadratic, and Exponential winners hold when the noise channel is non-Pauli (e.g. amplitude damping, coherent over-rotation, or a realistic IBM device Kraus map) rather than the simplified 2-qubit depolarizing model used in the paper and this replication?
basis: The paper (Fig. 6) and our 5-case reproduction both use depolarizing noise on CX gates only. Real hardware has amplitude damping, dephasing, coherent leakage, cross-talk, and non-Markovian drift. The mono-Exponential extrapolator's asymptote assumption (traceless observable decays to 0 under saturated depolarizing noise) is model-specific and may fail for amplitude damping or coherent noise.
next_steps: Rerun the 5-case grid on Mitiq with (a) a per-qubit amplitude-damping + dephasing channel calibrated from an IBM device backend snapshot, (b) a coherent-over-rotation error channel, and (c) the paper's original depolarizing model as control. Compare winner-family boundaries. Additionally, add asymptote-free ExpFactory (fit asymptote as parameter) and check whether it recovers robustness under non-depolarizing noise. All doable on Aer + free-tier IBM Quantum Open Plan; no paid endpoints needed.

q: How does dZNE best-practice interact with virtual distillation and probabilistic error cancellation when they are stacked as a QEM pipeline? Does the best extrapolation family per (depth, error-rate) cell shift when the raw observable has already been partially cleaned by distillation, and is there compounding benefit or diminishing returns?
basis: The paper Sec. V mentions composition with ROEM + Pauli twirling but does not treat virtual distillation (Huggins et al. 2021) or probabilistic error cancellation (Temme et al. 2017). Both are complementary QEM primitives; whether pre-distilled scans change the extrapolation-family winner is unstudied.
next_steps: Extend the 5-case harness: prepend virtual distillation (Mitiq's ddd module or a hand-rolled M-copy purification of the observable) to the raw scan, then run the same 4-family ZNE comparison. Repeat with PEC as an alternative pre-processor. Measure (i) whether Case D's narrow-range Richardson blow-up is tempered by pre-distillation and (ii) whether Case B's Exponential dominance survives. Free stack (Mitiq + Aer).

q: Can an adaptive per-circuit best-practice selector (choose extrapolation family and scale-factor range from a cheap circuit fingerprint such as 2q-gate-count, T-count, or a shallow noisy pilot scan) outperform the paper's static regime-based recommendation across a realistic benchmark suite?
basis: The paper's Fig. 6 gives a static (depth, error-rate) lookup table. In practice, circuit families with the same depth and same 2q-error rate can have very different observable saturation behavior (e.g. brickwork vs QAOA vs QPE), so the family winner may not be predictable from (depth, error) alone.
next_steps: Build a benchmark suite of 20-30 circuits spanning brickwork, QAOA, VQE ansatze, QPE, and random Clifford+T. For each circuit, run a 2-point pilot scan (lambda=1, 1.5) at 500 shots, compute the noisy-slope and curvature-proxy, then predict the best family via a simple decision rule. Compare against (a) always-Linear, (b) always-Exp, (c) paper static recommendation, (d) oracle best. Free Aer stack + optional Argo model for the decision-rule scoring.

q: What is the hardware-runtime overhead ratio of pulse-stretching noise scaling versus digital gate-folding on IBM Eagle-class devices for equivalent noise amplification, and does this overhead flip the best-practice recommendation when queue time and per-shot cost are included in the objective?
basis: The paper (and our replication) focuses on statistical accuracy (RMSE) as the sole quality metric. In practice, pulse stretching often requires OpenPulse access, custom calibration, and can be substantially slower per shot; digital folding is 3-5x more circuit depth for lambda=3-5 but uses stock transpilation.
next_steps: On IBM Quantum Open Plan (free), submit matched jobs: (a) digital fold at lambda in 1,3,5 and (b) pulse-stretched analog scaling at the same effective lambdas on the same device for a fixed test circuit. Measure wall-clock queue-to-result time, per-shot server-side execution time, and RMSE. Score by joint (RMSE, time-per-mitigated-observable). Aurora and Polaris HPC nodes not needed; this is pure IBM cloud.

q: Can a lightweight ML model (gradient-boosted tree or a small MLP) trained on offline (circuit-fingerprint, noise-fingerprint, family-winner) tuples learn to pick the best dZNE extrapolation family and scale-factor range with lower average RMSE than the paper's Fig. 6 lookup, and does the learned model transfer across device generations (Falcon vs Eagle vs Heron) without retraining?
basis: The paper offers a hand-crafted regime map. ML-driven QEM policy selection is a natural extension but has not been evaluated for ZNE family choice specifically. Cross-device transfer is the hard part: if the learned policy only works on the device it was trained on, the recommendation is not genuinely portable.
next_steps: Generate 500-1000 (circuit, noise-model, best-family) training tuples by running the 5-family bakeoff on randomly parameterized circuits under a range of depolarizing + amplitude-damping + coherent-error mixtures. Train an XGBoost classifier on 8 fingerprint features (2q depth, T-count, entangling-gate density, ideal-observable magnitude, pilot noisy-observable magnitude, pilot slope, pilot curvature, p2q estimate). Evaluate held-out RMSE vs paper lookup and vs oracle. Free compute: uicgpu A100 for training, Aer for tuple generation.
